text: {"entries":[{"name_han":"元始五老赤书玉篇真文天书经","logic_thesis":"This scripture proves that cosmic order is not merely descriptive mythology but is operationally encoded in sacred true-writings (真文): the five directions, five elders, and red-script jade chapters are the generative grammar by which chaos becomes differentiated cosmos. Authority to save and order the world therefore rests on correctly receiving, protecting, and deploying these graphs as causal instruments, not as symbols only. Salvation and cosmic repair follow from aligning human ritual with the same scriptural matrix that structured heaven and earth.","logic_chain":"1) Premises: the primordial void differentiates through fivefold directional powers under the Five Elders; true-writings are co-emergent with that differentiation. 2) Inference: if order is written into reality as 真文, then disorder is a failure of correct inscription/activation of that writing. 3) Inference: ritual transmission of the red-book jade chapters reinstalls the original ordering code. 4) Inference: those who hold the text legitimately participate in Yuanshi’s ordering power. 5) Conclusion: liturgical fidelity to the true-writings is the logical means of cosmic and personal rectification.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi, treat the five directions/five phases as a living ‘true-writing’ grid: map day-master and supporting stems to directional elders rather than as mere labels. 2) Use chart diagnosis as ‘misaligned inscription’—where qi clusters violate fivefold balance, prescribe corrective timing/ritual analogous to reactivating the corresponding 真文. 3) In cultivation, prioritize receiving and holding a pure transmission (lineage/text) before complex techniques. 4) Practice directional visualization of five colored scripts sealing the body as a microcosmic temple. 5) Time major life/ritual acts to stem-branch moments that reinforce the chart’s weakest directional phase.","logic_compare":"Unlike purely meditative neidan texts that interiorize the Dao as breath and mind, this scripture exteriorizes authority into revealed graphs and liturgical custody. It differs from later moral ledgers by grounding efficacy in cosmogonic writing rather than ethical scorekeeping. The argument is ontological-ritual: order is script, not merely virtue or quietude."},{"name_han":"性命圭旨","logic_thesis":"The text proves that complete realization requires dual cultivation of 性 (original nature/spirit) and 命 (embodied life-force/destiny), and that either alone is incomplete: empty quietism without life-refinement, or bodily alchemy without nature-illumination, both fail. It argues that the classical metaphors (kan-li, lead-mercury, dragon-tiger) are pedagogical maps of one reversible process uniting prenatal and postnatal. True ‘return’ is measurable as reintegration of nature and life into one original unity.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: human being is a split of 性 and 命 after birth. 2) Premise: pure nature-work without life-work leaves the body untransformed; pure life-work without nature-work remains energetic and dualistic. 3) Inference: the alchemical sequence must reverse the split in ordered stages (build foundation → gather → refine → unite). 4) Inference: symbolic language of yin-yang, five phases, and trigrams maps physiological-psychological operations. 5) Conclusion: liberation is the reunified 性命, not escape from the body or mere moral purity.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi, read 性 via day-master clarity/spirit indicators and 命 via resource, officer, and wealth structures as embodied constraints—then design dual practice. 2) Sequence training: first stabilize life (sleep, breath, jing conservation), then open nature (stillness, insight). 3) Use ten-gods imbalance as a diagnostic for whether the person needs more 命-work (earthly, circulatory, timing) or 性-work (mind, non-attachment). 4) Map luck pillars as seasons for which side of 性命 is easier to cultivate. 5) Treat ‘return to origin’ as concrete practice milestones, not slogans.","logic_compare":"Compared with early Shangqing visualization or pure precept scriptures, 性命圭旨 is systematically neidan and dualistic-to-nondual in method. It differs from 内观经’s simpler ‘look within’ by insisting on technical stages and life-force operations. Its uniqueness is the explicit thesis that incomplete half-cultivation is the main failure mode."},{"name_han":"道德会元","logic_thesis":"This work proves that the Daodejing’s apparent paradoxes resolve into a single metaphysical root (元): all teachings of non-action, softness, and emptiness are applications of returning to the undivided source rather than competing maxims. It argues that later schools diverge when they cling to partial phrases instead of the generative principle that unifies them. Correct interpretation is therefore reunification under the origin, not scholastic multiplication.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Dao is one origin; De is its functioning in the world. 2) Premise: classical sayings seem mutually tense (act/non-act, soft/hard, know/unknow). 3) Inference: tension dissolves if each saying is a situational expression of returning to 元. 4) Inference: misreading arises from treating rhetoric as independent doctrines. 5) Conclusion: the ‘assembly of origin’ is both exeegesis and spiritual method—gather scattered meanings and mind back to the source.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi counseling, reduce multi-factor noise to one core pattern (the chart’s ‘元’) before listing remedies. 2) When texts or techniques conflict, ask which practice restores simplicity rather than which is louder. 3) Cultivation: daily ‘return’ exercise—trace thoughts and desires back to the still point before action. 4) Prefer fewer, root-level corrections (seasonal living, breath, intention) over stacked rituals. 5) Use softness/non-contention strategically where the chart shows metal-wood clash or officer-killing pressure.","logic_compare":"Unlike 定观经 or 内观经, which prescribe specific contemplative procedures, 道德会元 is meta-hermeneutic: it proves a method of reading and unifying. It differs from 升玄内教经 by staying closer to Laozi’s philosophical root than to graded mystical ascent. Its distinctive claim is that fragmentation of doctrine is itself a spiritual disease."},{"name_han":"三天易髓","logic_thesis":"The text proves that the highest Daoist cosmology of the Three Heavens and the structural logic of the Yijing share one marrow (髓): change is not random but hierarchical, lawful, and reversible through correct alignment with celestial tiers. It argues that divinatory and liturgical order are two faces of one change-logic. Mastery means grasping the marrow of transformation, not memorizing surface hexagram lore or heavenly names alone.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: Three Heavens establish graded purity and authority in the cosmos. 2) Premise: Yijing encodes transformation through image, number, and position. 3) Inference: if both map lawful change, their ‘marrow’ is shared principles of rise-fall, yin-yang exchange, and timely positioning. 4) Inference: practice that unites heavenly rank with hexagram timing can steer fate. 5) Conclusion: the adept works at the marrow—principles of change—rather than outer form of either system.","logic_practice":"1) Read BaZi luck cycles as hexagram-like phase changes within a three-tier (heaven-earth-human) frame. 2) When advising on timing, combine stem-branch dynamics with image-number thinking (what is waxing/waning). 3) Cultivate by matching daily conduct to current ‘heaven’—clarity when upper qi dominates, restraint when turbid. 4) Use clash/combine events as change-nodes analogous to line transitions. 5) Drill one principle at a time (e.g., ‘extremes reverse’) across both chart cases and meditative observation.","logic_compare":"Unlike pure Yijing commentaries that stay in classical Confucian ethics, this text Daoicizes change under the Three Heavens hierarchy. It differs from 赤书真文经 by using change-marrow rather than sacred graphs as the operator. The argument privileges structural isomorphy between liturgy and divination."},{"name_han":"太上大通经","logic_thesis":"This short scripture proves that liberation is ‘great penetration’ (大通): the mind’s full openness in which barriers between self and Dao dissolve, not accumulation of merits or external powers. It argues that obstruction is cognitive-existential closure, so the path is progressive unblocking until free circulation of the Dao through the person. Realization is defined as unimpeded pervasion, not visionary spectacle.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the Dao is inherently pervasive and unobstructed. 2) Premise: humans suffer by self-contraction—desire, bias, fear. 3) Inference: practice that loosens contraction restores native pervasion. 4) Inference: when mind is fully open, distinctions that bind lose binding force. 5) Conclusion: attainment is 大通—great free passage—of Dao through body-mind.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi, locate ‘blockages’ as stuck ten-god patterns (e.g., heavy seals smothering output) and design practices that reopen circulation. 2) Meditation: sit for free-flow awareness without gripping states. 3) Daily: notice where speech, breath, or decision-making clamps; release one clamp. 4) Use luck-pillar shifts as times when previously closed chart channels can open. 5) Prefer methods that increase permeability (forgiveness, simplicity, breath) over forceful ‘breakthrough’ imagery when fire is already excessive.","logic_compare":"Compared with 定观经, which details stages of calming and insight, 大通经 states the end-state criterion: penetration itself. It is less moralistic than 百病百药经 and less administrative than 功过格. Its logic is soteriological-minimalist: open, and the Dao passes."},{"name_han":"太上老君中经","logic_thesis":"The Middle Scripture proves that the human body is a bureaucratic-cosmic double of heaven: visceral gods, palaces, and registers are not poetic decoration but the operational map of vitality and fate. It argues that health, longevity, and spiritual rank depend on correctly visualizing, naming, and retaining these inner officers. Loss of the gods is loss of life; retention is governance of the microcosm.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: heaven is ordered by named powers in hierarchical seats. 2) Premise: the body mirrors that order organ-by-organ and palace-by-palace. 3) Inference: disease and mortality reflect departure or dimming of inner gods. 4) Inference: visualization, recitation, and moral fitness re-seat the gods. 5) Conclusion: inner thearchy is the true ‘middle’ path between crude physiology and abstract mysticism.","logic_practice":"1) Map BaZi five-phase imbalances onto organ-god territories (e.g., weak earth → spleen/stomach court needs stabilization). 2) Practice daily retention: quiet sitting naming and illuminating key visceral deities. 3) Treat sleep, diet, and sexual conservation as ‘keeping the officers at court.’ 4) Use annual luck to schedule reinforcement of the weakest organ-phase. 5) When chart shows spirit disturbance (harsh kills, void, extreme fire), prioritize re-collecting the heart/spirit gods before external rites.","logic_compare":"Unlike 内观经’s more abstract mind-nature focus, 中经 is densely theurgical and anatomical-divine. It differs from external alchemy’s mineral work by locating the pantheon inside the body. The proof structure is microcosm-as-administration, not microcosm-as-mere-metaphor."},{"name_han":"太上除三尸九虫保生经","logic_thesis":"This scripture proves that premature death and spiritual failure are partly caused by endogenous parasites—the Three Corpses and Nine Worms—that report sins and erode vitality, so longevity is a hygienic-moral war against internal destroyers. It argues that fasting dates, drugs, spells, and ethical restraint work because they starve and expel these agents. Preservation of life is therefore simultaneous physiological purge and moral disarmament of the corpses’ accusations.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: within the body exist corpses/worms that feed on grain, desire, and fault. 2) Premise: they shorten life and betray the person to heavenly inspectors. 3) Inference: interrupting their food (gluttony, lust, chronic vice) weakens them. 4) Inference: timed rituals and remedies expel them when weakened. 5) Conclusion: 保生 is systematic elimination of internal saboteurs, not mere wish for long life.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi, heavy resource+wealth indulgence patterns may flag corpse-feeding lifestyles—prescribe abstinence cycles. 2) Observe traditional 庚申 watches or modern equivalents: all-night clarity to prevent corpse ascent. 3) Combine dietary simplification with confession/rectification of habits the worms ‘report.’ 4) Use metal and fire days for cutting/purging protocols when medically appropriate and lineage-authorized. 5) Track vitality after purge periods as empirical feedback, not superstition alone.","logic_compare":"Unlike 功过格, which scores deeds externally, this text internalizes the enemy as organisms of sin and decay. It differs from pure neidan’s sublimation language by retaining a parasitology of evil. Its logic is medical-demonological hybrid: ethics as anti-parasitic regimen."},{"name_han":"太上老君经律","logic_thesis":"The Precepts prove that Daoist identity is constituted by binding law (律): without communal and personal prohibitions, claimed cultivation is illegitimate and ineffective. Moral restraint is not optional ornament but the causal precondition for celestial recognition and inner stillness. The argument is that form (precept) enables formless attainment.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the Daoist community and the heavens operate by ordinance. 2) Premise: unregulated desire disorder both person and rite. 3) Inference: precepts define the boundary conditions of valid practice. 4) Inference: holding precepts purifies intent and invites spiritual response. 5) Conclusion: law is the gate of the Dao, not its opposite.","logic_practice":"1) Before advanced BaZi timing magic or ritual, install minimal precept set (no deceit, no reckless harm, sexual restraint as appropriate). 2) Use chart afflictions of officer/killing as signals needing more 律 (discipline) not more technique. 3) Weekly review: which precept leaks correlate with life chaos. 4) Teach clients that ‘luck changing’ without ethical container rebounds. 5) Align major vows with days of strong seal/resource for stability.","logic_compare":"Compared with 智慧罪根大戒经, this is more Laojun-authoritative and compactly disciplinary than elaborate Lingbao sin-root theory. It differs from 功过格 by stating norms rather than numeric accounting. The thesis is legal-foundational: no law, no Daoist subject."},{"name_han":"太上明鉴真经","logic_thesis":"The Bright Mirror Scripture proves that true seeing is achieved by making the mind a luminous mirror: spirits, forms, and destinies become knowable when the reflective surface is polished of dust. It argues that clarity is an optical-spiritual condition, not intellectual accumulation. Divination, self-knowledge, and theophany share one mechanism—undefiled reflection.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: reality can appear in a pure reflective medium. 2) Premise: passion and turbidity are dust on the mirror. 3) Inference: polishing (stillness, purity, correct method) restores reflection. 4) Inference: with reflection restored, hidden beings and patterns show. 5) Conclusion: ‘bright mirror’ is both practice and epistemic criterion of truth.","logic_practice":"1) BaZi reading posture: empty the mirror before interpreting—bias is dust. 2) Train short ‘mirror sits’: pure awareness without commentary, then look at the chart. 3) Use water-rich chart periods for scrying-like introspection; use metal for decisive polishing (cutting delusion). 4) When clients demand flattering readings, refuse—distorted mirror is false scripture. 5) Evening review: what emotional dust entered today, wipe once.","logic_compare":"Unlike 内观经, which emphasizes inspecting the inner landscape of Dao-nature, 明鉴 stresses the optical metaphor of reflection and often theurgical seeing. It differs from 定观经 by focusing less on staged calming taxonomy and more on luminous epistemic purity. The logic is mirror-epistemology as salvation tech."},{"name_han":"太微仙君功过格","logic_thesis":"The Merit-Demerit Ledger proves that destiny is partly computable: actions generate quantifiable credits and debits that determine fortune, lifespan, and spiritual rank. It argues that vague aspiration is inferior to daily metric self-audit under celestial bureaucracy. Moral life becomes an accounting system whose balances causally shape fate.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: heaven records deeds with precision. 2) Premise: good and bad acts differ in weight and can be scaled. 3) Inference: a personal ledger makes the invisible record visible and trainable. 4) Inference: net surplus of merit improves outcomes; deficit invites misfortune. 5) Conclusion: systematic self-scoring is a technology of fate repair.","logic_practice":"1) Build a simple daily 功过 grid (speech, sex, anger, generosity, deceit). 2) In BaZi years of clash/punishment, increase merit protocols deliberately. 3) Convert abstract ‘be better’ into point targets tied to the chart’s weak virtues (e.g., weak wood → benevolent acts). 4) Monthly reconcile: which demerits cluster with ten-god stress patterns. 5) Never use points as pride currency—audit is mirror, not trophy.","logic_compare":"Unlike precept texts that state ‘do not,’ 功过格 operationalizes morality as numeric feedback. It differs from corpse-worm texts by focusing on externalizable deeds rather than internal parasites. Its distinctive logic is managerial ethics: what gets measured gets transformed."},{"name_han":"高上玉皇本行集经","logic_thesis":"This scripture proves that supreme celestial authority (the Jade Emperor) is grounded in a narrative of perfected practice, vows, and salvific career—not arbitrary power. It argues that reciting and venerating the Emperor’s original deeds aligns the devotee with the cosmic throne’s legitimacy and mercy. Hierarchy is justified by demonstrated universal compassion and cultivation history.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: cosmic rule requires a sovereign of heaven. 2) Premise: that sovereign’s legitimacy is shown through past practice and vows for beings. 3) Inference: recalling the ‘original deeds’ transfers that legitimacy into present devotion. 4) Inference: aligned devotees receive protection and status under that throne. 5) Conclusion: hagiography is soteriological technology, not mere biography.","logic_practice":"1) Use recitation in periods when BaZi shows authority crisis (hurt officer, chaos of kills). 2) Frame personal cultivation as vow-career modeled on the text’s arc, not isolated tricks. 3) For clients with weak or broken ‘officer’ structures, rebuild healthy relationship to lawful authority via ritual respect rather than rebellion. 4) Combine liturgy with concrete compassionate acts to match the text’s logic. 5) Time major vows to days of strong heaven-stem clarity.","logic_compare":"Compared with abstract Laozi cosmogony, this is imperial-hagiographic: power justified by holy career. It differs from Lingbao precept sutras by centering a sovereign personhood of heaven. The argument links narrative memory to present grace under cosmic monarchy."},{"name_han":"太上洞玄灵宝智慧罪根上品大戒经","logic_thesis":"This Lingbao text proves that sin has roots (罪根)—deep causal structures of ignorance and habit—and that superior precepts are surgical tools of wisdom cutting those roots, not mere social etiquette. It argues that without root-cutting discipline, ritual and knowledge remain ornamental. Wisdom (智慧) and precept (戒) are one act of liberation.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: suffering and impurity arise from rooted causes, not isolated mistakes. 2) Premise: ordinary restraint trims branches; superior precepts target roots. 3) Inference: holding high precepts with understanding severs generative patterns of fault. 4) Inference: once roots are cut, higher Lingbao wisdom can function. 5) Conclusion: ethical-wisdom fusion is the upper path of sin-eradication.","logic_practice":"1) Diagnose BaZi ‘sin roots’ as recurring harmful configurations (e.g., perpetual peer-rivalry 比劫 stealing wealth → greed/jealousy loops). 2) Assign one root precept per loop, not ten vague rules. 3) Study why the precept liberates (wisdom) while holding it (戒). 4) Use retreat days in heavy earth/seal months for root examination. 5) Measure success by recurrence rate of the pattern, not by self-image.","logic_compare":"Unlike 老君经律’s more general disciplinary framing, this text theorizes 罪根 and elevates precept to wisdom-operation. It differs from 百病百药经’s disease metaphor by using botanical-causal ‘root’ logic. Its specificity is Lingbao soteriology: wisdom-precept as dual blade."},{"name_han":"太上老君说百病崇百药经","logic_thesis":"The text proves that moral and psychological faults are true diseases (病) and that corrective virtues/behaviors are medicines (药), establishing a clinical ethics: diagnosis must match remedy. It argues that people fail because they misidentify the illness or take the wrong moral drug. Health of character is treated with the same rigor as bodily medicine.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: vices and imbalances present with recognizable syndromes. 2) Premise: each syndrome has a corresponding corrective practice. 3) Inference: cataloging hundred diseases/medicines enables precise treatment. 4) Inference: wrong remedy (e.g., more hardness for anger-heat) worsens the case. 5) Conclusion: ethical life is differential therapeutics under Laojun’s clinical teaching.","logic_practice":"1) Translate BaZi excesses into disease names (excess fire → irritability disease; weak water → fear/insufficiency disease). 2) Prescribe matching ‘medicines’ (gentleness, generosity, stillness) with dosage and duration. 3) Avoid one-size-fits-all virtue lists. 4) Reassess after one lunar month like a follow-up clinic. 5) Combine with physical hygiene when the chart links organ-phase to the moral symptom.","logic_compare":"Unlike 功过格’s point economy, this is pharmacological: match drug to disease. It differs from corpse-worm texts by treating faults as syndromes rather than parasites. The logical novelty is systematic moral nosology and pharmacy."},{"name_han":"太上洞玄灵宝升玄内教经","logic_thesis":"This scripture proves that ultimate teaching is ‘inner teaching’ (内教) of ascending to mystery (升玄): outer rites and names are provisional rungs toward a more secret, interiorized ascent. It argues that progression is graded—exoteric to esoteric—and that clinging to outer forms blocks the rise. True Lingbao culminates in interior mystery, not endless external performance.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: beings differ in capacity; teaching must be staged. 2) Premise: outer liturgy trains and purifies but is not the end. 3) Inference: at maturity, meaning migrates inward as 内教. 4) Inference: ascent to 玄 is loss of coarse grasping including grasping of the path’s shell. 5) Conclusion: salvation logic is pedagogical ascent from outer to inner mystery.","logic_practice":"1) Structure BaZi-guided cultivation in grades: ethics → breath/body → silent mystery. 2) When a client’s chart is ripe (strong resource+output, stable mind markers), shift from ritual quantity to inner quality. 3) Detect ‘stuck on form’ as a new obstacle after early success. 4) Use transitional luck pillars to retire obsolete methods. 5) Keep outer respect for liturgy while not equating it with the summit.","logic_compare":"Compared with 赤书真文经’s emphasis on cosmic graphs and liturgy, 升玄内教 argues for interiorizing beyond outer codes. It differs from pure neidan manuals by retaining Lingbao graded-church pedagogy. The key thesis is esoteric ascent as curriculum, not denial of the outer."},{"name_han":"洞玄灵宝定观经","logic_thesis":"The Dingguan Jing proves that liberation follows a law of settled contemplation: first stabilize (定), then observe (观), such that clarity arises from stillness rather than from forced insight. It argues that scattered seeking produces false visions, while correct sequence yields genuine detachment and brightness. Method-order is salvific cause.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the ordinary mind is agitated and mis-sees. 2) Premise: agitation cannot be cured by more conceptual striving. 3) Inference: settle the mind until it holds. 4) Inference: from stability, observation becomes accurate and self-liberating. 5) Conclusion: 定→观 is the necessary logical order of contemplative proof.","logic_practice":"1) For high-fire or kill-heavy BaZi, emphasize 定 first (breath counting, posture) before analysis. 2) For overly sealed/stagnant charts, carefully introduce 观 after minimal stability to avoid dullness. 3) Session design: 2/3 settling, 1/3 observing for beginners. 4) Chart readings only after the reader’s own 定. 5) Track signs: fewer reactive emotions as proof of genuine 定观, not more mystical stories.","logic_compare":"Unlike 大通经’s brief end-state language, 定观经 specifies the causal sequence of practice. It differs from 明鉴’s mirror imagery by stressing stages of calming before illumined seeing. Its contribution is methodological order as doctrine."},{"name_han":"太上虚皇天尊四十九章经","logic_thesis":"The Forty-nine Chapters prove that the Dao’s teaching can be exhaustively modularized into discrete instructional units, each addressing a facet of mind, world, and liberation under the Xu Huang Heavenly Worthy. It argues that completeness is achieved by traversing a structured curriculum rather than a single slogan. Multiplicity of chapters serves one empty-sovereign source.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: beings’ confusions are many-sided. 2) Premise: a single undifferentiated teaching fails specific diseases of mind. 3) Inference: chaptered instruction covers the field systematically. 4) Inference: practicing chapter by chapter accumulates toward total reorientation. 5) Conclusion: structured plurality is skillful means of the formless 虚皇.","logic_practice":"1) Map 49 thematic modules onto a year-long cultivation calendar. 2) Assign chapters to BaZi weak points (anger chapters for fire excess, etc.). 3) Do not skip to ‘advanced’ chapters without foundation modules. 4) After each chapter-practice, write one behavioral proof. 5) Periodically return to emptiness chapters to prevent modular reification.","logic_compare":"Unlike short texts such as 大通经, this work’s logic is encyclopedic pedagogy. It differs from 功过格 by teaching transformative views/practices rather than scoring acts. The distinct claim is curriculum completeness under an empty-imperial deity."},{"name_han":"太上玄都妙本清净身心经","logic_thesis":"This scripture proves that purity of body and mind is recovery of the ‘wondrous root’ (妙本) at the Mysterious Capital—not cosmetic cleanliness. It argues that defilement is adventitious; cleansing reveals the already-pure base. Dual purification (physical and mental) is required because impurity couples across body-mind.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the original root is pure. 2) Premise: postnatal dust settles on body and mind together. 3) Inference: one-sided cleansing (body only or mind only) leaves residual stain. 4) Inference: coordinated purity restores access to 妙本. 5) Conclusion: 清净身心 is ontological recovery, not social hygiene.","logic_practice":"1) Pair hygienic routines with mental confession/release as one protocol. 2) In BaZi toxicity patterns (heavy killing+peer, or wet earth turbidity), design purification seasons. 3) Use simple food, breath, and ethical speech as triple filter. 4) Before major luck-pillar shifts, run a purity retreat to meet new qi cleanly. 5) Evaluate purity by reduced inner noise and fewer self-conflicts, not by performative asceticism.","logic_compare":"Compared with 除三尸经, the enemy here is defilement-as-dust rather than parasites. It differs from 内观经 by stressing dual body-mind cleansing toward a named 妙本. The logic is root-recovery via purity rather than vision of gods or numeric merit."},{"name_han":"黄帝九鼎神丹经诀","logic_thesis":"The Nine Cauldron instructions prove that immortality can be engineered through correct external alchemy: materials, fire phases, timing, and vessel order are causal, not mystical wish. It argues that the elixir’s success encodes cosmic process in laboratory operations—failure is procedural error. Transcendence is a technical achievement under Huang-Lao authority.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: minerals and fire can be transmuted under lawlike stages. 2) Premise: the nine-鼎 sequence mirrors perfected cosmic refinement. 3) Inference: precise protocol yields shendan; imprecision yields poison or null. 4) Inference: the perfected elixir transforms the human body-economy. 5) Conclusion: sacred techne is a valid path of transcendence alongside pure meditation.","logic_practice":"1) Read BaZi as ‘furnace conditions’: what fire (motivation/timing), what vessel (constitution), what materials (resources) you have. 2) Apply staged patience—do not jump refining phases in life projects. 3) For modern practitioners, translate external elixir logic into laboratory discipline of sleep, diet, herbs only under safe expertise—or into symbolic neidan firing cycles. 4) Use seasonal nodes as ‘fire times.’ 5) Document each stage; alchemy without records is not alchemy.","logic_compare":"Unlike 性命圭旨’s internalized dual cultivation, this text centers external laboratory causality. It differs from pure precept or contemplation scriptures by making matter and fire the argument’s heroes. Its logic is operative cosmotechnology rather than moral or purely mental soteriology."},{"name_han":"太上老君内观经","logic_thesis":"The Scripture of Inner Contemplation proves that the Dao is found by turning the gaze inward: the body-mind contains the entire field of spirit, and outer seeking multiplies delusion. It argues that correct 内观 reveals emptiness, spirit, and life as already present, converting metaphysics into a perceptual practice. Knowing the Dao is a change of direction of attention.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: the Dao is not a remote object among objects. 2) Premise: outward chase reinforces the split between seeker and sought. 3) Inference: reverse the gaze into the inner domain of spirit and vitality. 4) Inference: sustained inner seeing clarifies original nature and calms destiny-chaos. 5) Conclusion: 内观 is both method and proof of the Dao’s immanence.","logic_practice":"1) Daily reverse-attention drill: from senses → breath → spirit → open awareness. 2) In BaZi counseling, teach clients to observe their chart patterns as inner habits, not only outer events. 3) When 七杀/伤官 agitation is high, use 内观 to metabolize heat before action. 4) Alternate brief outer ritual with longer inner viewing to avoid dependence on spectacle. 5) Criterion of progress: less compulsion to seek signs outside.","logic_compare":"Unlike 中经’s detailed deity bureaucracy, 内观经 is leaner and more nature-of-mind oriented. It differs from 定观经 by emphasizing the inward turn as such more than the formal 定/观 taxonomy. The core argument is directional: truth is missed by vector, not by lack of information."},{"name_han":"太上正一咒鬼经","logic_thesis":"This Zhengyi scripture proves that disruptive agencies (鬼) are real operational factors in illness and chaos, and that correctly authorized spells can command, bind, or expel them. It argues that ritual speech under Zhengyi mandate is not poetry but executive force within a legal-spiritual order. Order is restored when illegitimate spirits are brought under lawful spell-authority.","logic_chain":"1) Premise: many disorders involve intrusive or aggrieved spirit-agencies. 2) Premise: the Zhengyi covenant grants priests command language backed by higher law. 3) Inference: properly formed 咒 apply that law to specific agents. 4) Inference: successful binding/expulsion restores human and communal equilibrium. 5) Conclusion: exorcistic speech is a legitimate causal technology of the Zhengyi path.","logic_practice":"1) In BaZi, treat extreme, sudden, anomalous afflictions during void/clash years as candidates for spirit-related differential diagnosis—without neglecting medical care. 2) Only practice spells with lineage authorization; unauthorized imitation breaks the text’s own logic of mandate. 3) Pair expulsions with merit and purification so the vacuum is not refilled. 4) Strengthen the day-master’s ‘right authority’ (healthy officer/seal) as the human side of Zhengyi order. 5) Post-rite, install stable daily regimen; exorcism without re-ordering lifestyle is incomplete.","logic_compare":"Unlike 内观/定观 contemplative proofs, this text is juridical-exorcistic: power is command under covenant. It differs from 除三尸经 by targeting mostly external/intrusive agencies rather than innate corpses. Its distinctive logic is performative sacred law—speech acts that enforce cosmic police power."}]}

entries.name_han: 元始五老赤书玉篇真文天书经
entries.logic_thesis: This scripture proves that cosmic order is not merely descriptive mythology but is operationally encoded in sacred true-writings (真文): the five directions, five elders, and red-script jade chapters are the generative grammar by which chaos becomes differentiated cosmos. Authority to save and order the world therefore rests on correctly receiving, protecting, and deploying these graphs as causal instruments, not as symbols only. Salvation and cosmic repair follow from aligning human ritual with the same scriptural matrix that structured heaven and earth.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premises: the primordial void differentiates through fivefold directional powers under the Five Elders; true-writings are co-emergent with that differentiation. 2) Inference: if order is written into reality as 真文, then disorder is a failure of correct inscription/activation of that writing. 3) Inference: ritual transmission of the red-book jade chapters reinstalls the original ordering code. 4) Inference: those who hold the text legitimately participate in Yuanshi’s ordering power. 5) Conclusion: liturgical fidelity to the true-writings is the logical means of cosmic and personal rectification.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, treat the five directions/five phases as a living ‘true-writing’ grid: map day-master and supporting stems to directional elders rather than as mere labels. 2) Use chart diagnosis as ‘misaligned inscription’—where qi clusters violate fivefold balance, prescribe corrective timing/ritual analogous to reactivating the corresponding 真文. 3) In cultivation, prioritize receiving and holding a pure transmission (lineage/text) before complex techniques. 4) Practice directional visualization of five colored scripts sealing the body as a microcosmic temple. 5) Time major life/ritual acts to stem-branch moments that reinforce the chart’s weakest directional phase.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike purely meditative neidan texts that interiorize the Dao as breath and mind, this scripture exteriorizes authority into revealed graphs and liturgical custody. It differs from later moral ledgers by grounding efficacy in cosmogonic writing rather than ethical scorekeeping. The argument is ontological-ritual: order is script, not merely virtue or quietude.

entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that complete realization requires dual cultivation of 性 (original nature/spirit) and 命 (embodied life-force/destiny), and that either alone is incomplete: empty quietism without life-refinement, or bodily alchemy without nature-illumination, both fail. It argues that the classical metaphors (kan-li, lead-mercury, dragon-tiger) are pedagogical maps of one reversible process uniting prenatal and postnatal. True ‘return’ is measurable as reintegration of nature and life into one original unity.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: human being is a split of 性 and 命 after birth. 2) Premise: pure nature-work without life-work leaves the body untransformed; pure life-work without nature-work remains energetic and dualistic. 3) Inference: the alchemical sequence must reverse the split in ordered stages (build foundation → gather → refine → unite). 4) Inference: symbolic language of yin-yang, five phases, and trigrams maps physiological-psychological operations. 5) Conclusion: liberation is the reunified 性命, not escape from the body or mere moral purity.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, read 性 via day-master clarity/spirit indicators and 命 via resource, officer, and wealth structures as embodied constraints—then design dual practice. 2) Sequence training: first stabilize life (sleep, breath, jing conservation), then open nature (stillness, insight). 3) Use ten-gods imbalance as a diagnostic for whether the person needs more 命-work (earthly, circulatory, timing) or 性-work (mind, non-attachment). 4) Map luck pillars as seasons for which side of 性命 is easier to cultivate. 5) Treat ‘return to origin’ as concrete practice milestones, not slogans.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with early Shangqing visualization or pure precept scriptures, 性命圭旨 is systematically neidan and dualistic-to-nondual in method. It differs from 内观经’s simpler ‘look within’ by insisting on technical stages and life-force operations. Its uniqueness is the explicit thesis that incomplete half-cultivation is the main failure mode.

entries.logic_thesis: This work proves that the Daodejing’s apparent paradoxes resolve into a single metaphysical root (元): all teachings of non-action, softness, and emptiness are applications of returning to the undivided source rather than competing maxims. It argues that later schools diverge when they cling to partial phrases instead of the generative principle that unifies them. Correct interpretation is therefore reunification under the origin, not scholastic multiplication.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Dao is one origin; De is its functioning in the world. 2) Premise: classical sayings seem mutually tense (act/non-act, soft/hard, know/unknow). 3) Inference: tension dissolves if each saying is a situational expression of returning to 元. 4) Inference: misreading arises from treating rhetoric as independent doctrines. 5) Conclusion: the ‘assembly of origin’ is both exeegesis and spiritual method—gather scattered meanings and mind back to the source.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi counseling, reduce multi-factor noise to one core pattern (the chart’s ‘元’) before listing remedies. 2) When texts or techniques conflict, ask which practice restores simplicity rather than which is louder. 3) Cultivation: daily ‘return’ exercise—trace thoughts and desires back to the still point before action. 4) Prefer fewer, root-level corrections (seasonal living, breath, intention) over stacked rituals. 5) Use softness/non-contention strategically where the chart shows metal-wood clash or officer-killing pressure.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 定观经 or 内观经, which prescribe specific contemplative procedures, 道德会元 is meta-hermeneutic: it proves a method of reading and unifying. It differs from 升玄内教经 by staying closer to Laozi’s philosophical root than to graded mystical ascent. Its distinctive claim is that fragmentation of doctrine is itself a spiritual disease.

entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that the highest Daoist cosmology of the Three Heavens and the structural logic of the Yijing share one marrow (髓): change is not random but hierarchical, lawful, and reversible through correct alignment with celestial tiers. It argues that divinatory and liturgical order are two faces of one change-logic. Mastery means grasping the marrow of transformation, not memorizing surface hexagram lore or heavenly names alone.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: Three Heavens establish graded purity and authority in the cosmos. 2) Premise: Yijing encodes transformation through image, number, and position. 3) Inference: if both map lawful change, their ‘marrow’ is shared principles of rise-fall, yin-yang exchange, and timely positioning. 4) Inference: practice that unites heavenly rank with hexagram timing can steer fate. 5) Conclusion: the adept works at the marrow—principles of change—rather than outer form of either system.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Read BaZi luck cycles as hexagram-like phase changes within a three-tier (heaven-earth-human) frame. 2) When advising on timing, combine stem-branch dynamics with image-number thinking (what is waxing/waning). 3) Cultivate by matching daily conduct to current ‘heaven’—clarity when upper qi dominates, restraint when turbid. 4) Use clash/combine events as change-nodes analogous to line transitions. 5) Drill one principle at a time (e.g., ‘extremes reverse’) across both chart cases and meditative observation.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure Yijing commentaries that stay in classical Confucian ethics, this text Daoicizes change under the Three Heavens hierarchy. It differs from 赤书真文经 by using change-marrow rather than sacred graphs as the operator. The argument privileges structural isomorphy between liturgy and divination.

entries.logic_thesis: This short scripture proves that liberation is ‘great penetration’ (大通): the mind’s full openness in which barriers between self and Dao dissolve, not accumulation of merits or external powers. It argues that obstruction is cognitive-existential closure, so the path is progressive unblocking until free circulation of the Dao through the person. Realization is defined as unimpeded pervasion, not visionary spectacle.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the Dao is inherently pervasive and unobstructed. 2) Premise: humans suffer by self-contraction—desire, bias, fear. 3) Inference: practice that loosens contraction restores native pervasion. 4) Inference: when mind is fully open, distinctions that bind lose binding force. 5) Conclusion: attainment is 大通—great free passage—of Dao through body-mind.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, locate ‘blockages’ as stuck ten-god patterns (e.g., heavy seals smothering output) and design practices that reopen circulation. 2) Meditation: sit for free-flow awareness without gripping states. 3) Daily: notice where speech, breath, or decision-making clamps; release one clamp. 4) Use luck-pillar shifts as times when previously closed chart channels can open. 5) Prefer methods that increase permeability (forgiveness, simplicity, breath) over forceful ‘breakthrough’ imagery when fire is already excessive.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 定观经, which details stages of calming and insight, 大通经 states the end-state criterion: penetration itself. It is less moralistic than 百病百药经 and less administrative than 功过格. Its logic is soteriological-minimalist: open, and the Dao passes.

entries.logic_thesis: The Middle Scripture proves that the human body is a bureaucratic-cosmic double of heaven: visceral gods, palaces, and registers are not poetic decoration but the operational map of vitality and fate. It argues that health, longevity, and spiritual rank depend on correctly visualizing, naming, and retaining these inner officers. Loss of the gods is loss of life; retention is governance of the microcosm.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: heaven is ordered by named powers in hierarchical seats. 2) Premise: the body mirrors that order organ-by-organ and palace-by-palace. 3) Inference: disease and mortality reflect departure or dimming of inner gods. 4) Inference: visualization, recitation, and moral fitness re-seat the gods. 5) Conclusion: inner thearchy is the true ‘middle’ path between crude physiology and abstract mysticism.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Map BaZi five-phase imbalances onto organ-god territories (e.g., weak earth → spleen/stomach court needs stabilization). 2) Practice daily retention: quiet sitting naming and illuminating key visceral deities. 3) Treat sleep, diet, and sexual conservation as ‘keeping the officers at court.’ 4) Use annual luck to schedule reinforcement of the weakest organ-phase. 5) When chart shows spirit disturbance (harsh kills, void, extreme fire), prioritize re-collecting the heart/spirit gods before external rites.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 内观经’s more abstract mind-nature focus, 中经 is densely theurgical and anatomical-divine. It differs from external alchemy’s mineral work by locating the pantheon inside the body. The proof structure is microcosm-as-administration, not microcosm-as-mere-metaphor.

entries.name_han: 太上除三尸九虫保生经
entries.logic_thesis: This scripture proves that premature death and spiritual failure are partly caused by endogenous parasites—the Three Corpses and Nine Worms—that report sins and erode vitality, so longevity is a hygienic-moral war against internal destroyers. It argues that fasting dates, drugs, spells, and ethical restraint work because they starve and expel these agents. Preservation of life is therefore simultaneous physiological purge and moral disarmament of the corpses’ accusations.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: within the body exist corpses/worms that feed on grain, desire, and fault. 2) Premise: they shorten life and betray the person to heavenly inspectors. 3) Inference: interrupting their food (gluttony, lust, chronic vice) weakens them. 4) Inference: timed rituals and remedies expel them when weakened. 5) Conclusion: 保生 is systematic elimination of internal saboteurs, not mere wish for long life.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, heavy resource+wealth indulgence patterns may flag corpse-feeding lifestyles—prescribe abstinence cycles. 2) Observe traditional 庚申 watches or modern equivalents: all-night clarity to prevent corpse ascent. 3) Combine dietary simplification with confession/rectification of habits the worms ‘report.’ 4) Use metal and fire days for cutting/purging protocols when medically appropriate and lineage-authorized. 5) Track vitality after purge periods as empirical feedback, not superstition alone.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 功过格, which scores deeds externally, this text internalizes the enemy as organisms of sin and decay. It differs from pure neidan’s sublimation language by retaining a parasitology of evil. Its logic is medical-demonological hybrid: ethics as anti-parasitic regimen.

entries.logic_thesis: The Precepts prove that Daoist identity is constituted by binding law (律): without communal and personal prohibitions, claimed cultivation is illegitimate and ineffective. Moral restraint is not optional ornament but the causal precondition for celestial recognition and inner stillness. The argument is that form (precept) enables formless attainment.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the Daoist community and the heavens operate by ordinance. 2) Premise: unregulated desire disorder both person and rite. 3) Inference: precepts define the boundary conditions of valid practice. 4) Inference: holding precepts purifies intent and invites spiritual response. 5) Conclusion: law is the gate of the Dao, not its opposite.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before advanced BaZi timing magic or ritual, install minimal precept set (no deceit, no reckless harm, sexual restraint as appropriate). 2) Use chart afflictions of officer/killing as signals needing more 律 (discipline) not more technique. 3) Weekly review: which precept leaks correlate with life chaos. 4) Teach clients that ‘luck changing’ without ethical container rebounds. 5) Align major vows with days of strong seal/resource for stability.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 智慧罪根大戒经, this is more Laojun-authoritative and compactly disciplinary than elaborate Lingbao sin-root theory. It differs from 功过格 by stating norms rather than numeric accounting. The thesis is legal-foundational: no law, no Daoist subject.

entries.logic_thesis: The Bright Mirror Scripture proves that true seeing is achieved by making the mind a luminous mirror: spirits, forms, and destinies become knowable when the reflective surface is polished of dust. It argues that clarity is an optical-spiritual condition, not intellectual accumulation. Divination, self-knowledge, and theophany share one mechanism—undefiled reflection.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: reality can appear in a pure reflective medium. 2) Premise: passion and turbidity are dust on the mirror. 3) Inference: polishing (stillness, purity, correct method) restores reflection. 4) Inference: with reflection restored, hidden beings and patterns show. 5) Conclusion: ‘bright mirror’ is both practice and epistemic criterion of truth.
entries.logic_practice: 1) BaZi reading posture: empty the mirror before interpreting—bias is dust. 2) Train short ‘mirror sits’: pure awareness without commentary, then look at the chart. 3) Use water-rich chart periods for scrying-like introspection; use metal for decisive polishing (cutting delusion). 4) When clients demand flattering readings, refuse—distorted mirror is false scripture. 5) Evening review: what emotional dust entered today, wipe once.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 内观经, which emphasizes inspecting the inner landscape of Dao-nature, 明鉴 stresses the optical metaphor of reflection and often theurgical seeing. It differs from 定观经 by focusing less on staged calming taxonomy and more on luminous epistemic purity. The logic is mirror-epistemology as salvation tech.

entries.logic_thesis: The Merit-Demerit Ledger proves that destiny is partly computable: actions generate quantifiable credits and debits that determine fortune, lifespan, and spiritual rank. It argues that vague aspiration is inferior to daily metric self-audit under celestial bureaucracy. Moral life becomes an accounting system whose balances causally shape fate.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: heaven records deeds with precision. 2) Premise: good and bad acts differ in weight and can be scaled. 3) Inference: a personal ledger makes the invisible record visible and trainable. 4) Inference: net surplus of merit improves outcomes; deficit invites misfortune. 5) Conclusion: systematic self-scoring is a technology of fate repair.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Build a simple daily 功过 grid (speech, sex, anger, generosity, deceit). 2) In BaZi years of clash/punishment, increase merit protocols deliberately. 3) Convert abstract ‘be better’ into point targets tied to the chart’s weak virtues (e.g., weak wood → benevolent acts). 4) Monthly reconcile: which demerits cluster with ten-god stress patterns. 5) Never use points as pride currency—audit is mirror, not trophy.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike precept texts that state ‘do not,’ 功过格 operationalizes morality as numeric feedback. It differs from corpse-worm texts by focusing on externalizable deeds rather than internal parasites. Its distinctive logic is managerial ethics: what gets measured gets transformed.

entries.logic_thesis: This scripture proves that supreme celestial authority (the Jade Emperor) is grounded in a narrative of perfected practice, vows, and salvific career—not arbitrary power. It argues that reciting and venerating the Emperor’s original deeds aligns the devotee with the cosmic throne’s legitimacy and mercy. Hierarchy is justified by demonstrated universal compassion and cultivation history.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: cosmic rule requires a sovereign of heaven. 2) Premise: that sovereign’s legitimacy is shown through past practice and vows for beings. 3) Inference: recalling the ‘original deeds’ transfers that legitimacy into present devotion. 4) Inference: aligned devotees receive protection and status under that throne. 5) Conclusion: hagiography is soteriological technology, not mere biography.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Use recitation in periods when BaZi shows authority crisis (hurt officer, chaos of kills). 2) Frame personal cultivation as vow-career modeled on the text’s arc, not isolated tricks. 3) For clients with weak or broken ‘officer’ structures, rebuild healthy relationship to lawful authority via ritual respect rather than rebellion. 4) Combine liturgy with concrete compassionate acts to match the text’s logic. 5) Time major vows to days of strong heaven-stem clarity.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with abstract Laozi cosmogony, this is imperial-hagiographic: power justified by holy career. It differs from Lingbao precept sutras by centering a sovereign personhood of heaven. The argument links narrative memory to present grace under cosmic monarchy.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄灵宝智慧罪根上品大戒经
entries.logic_thesis: This Lingbao text proves that sin has roots (罪根)—deep causal structures of ignorance and habit—and that superior precepts are surgical tools of wisdom cutting those roots, not mere social etiquette. It argues that without root-cutting discipline, ritual and knowledge remain ornamental. Wisdom (智慧) and precept (戒) are one act of liberation.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: suffering and impurity arise from rooted causes, not isolated mistakes. 2) Premise: ordinary restraint trims branches; superior precepts target roots. 3) Inference: holding high precepts with understanding severs generative patterns of fault. 4) Inference: once roots are cut, higher Lingbao wisdom can function. 5) Conclusion: ethical-wisdom fusion is the upper path of sin-eradication.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Diagnose BaZi ‘sin roots’ as recurring harmful configurations (e.g., perpetual peer-rivalry 比劫 stealing wealth → greed/jealousy loops). 2) Assign one root precept per loop, not ten vague rules. 3) Study why the precept liberates (wisdom) while holding it (戒). 4) Use retreat days in heavy earth/seal months for root examination. 5) Measure success by recurrence rate of the pattern, not by self-image.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 老君经律’s more general disciplinary framing, this text theorizes 罪根 and elevates precept to wisdom-operation. It differs from 百病百药经’s disease metaphor by using botanical-causal ‘root’ logic. Its specificity is Lingbao soteriology: wisdom-precept as dual blade.

entries.name_han: 太上老君说百病崇百药经
entries.logic_thesis: The text proves that moral and psychological faults are true diseases (病) and that corrective virtues/behaviors are medicines (药), establishing a clinical ethics: diagnosis must match remedy. It argues that people fail because they misidentify the illness or take the wrong moral drug. Health of character is treated with the same rigor as bodily medicine.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: vices and imbalances present with recognizable syndromes. 2) Premise: each syndrome has a corresponding corrective practice. 3) Inference: cataloging hundred diseases/medicines enables precise treatment. 4) Inference: wrong remedy (e.g., more hardness for anger-heat) worsens the case. 5) Conclusion: ethical life is differential therapeutics under Laojun’s clinical teaching.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Translate BaZi excesses into disease names (excess fire → irritability disease; weak water → fear/insufficiency disease). 2) Prescribe matching ‘medicines’ (gentleness, generosity, stillness) with dosage and duration. 3) Avoid one-size-fits-all virtue lists. 4) Reassess after one lunar month like a follow-up clinic. 5) Combine with physical hygiene when the chart links organ-phase to the moral symptom.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 功过格’s point economy, this is pharmacological: match drug to disease. It differs from corpse-worm texts by treating faults as syndromes rather than parasites. The logical novelty is systematic moral nosology and pharmacy.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄灵宝升玄内教经
entries.logic_thesis: This scripture proves that ultimate teaching is ‘inner teaching’ (内教) of ascending to mystery (升玄): outer rites and names are provisional rungs toward a more secret, interiorized ascent. It argues that progression is graded—exoteric to esoteric—and that clinging to outer forms blocks the rise. True Lingbao culminates in interior mystery, not endless external performance.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: beings differ in capacity; teaching must be staged. 2) Premise: outer liturgy trains and purifies but is not the end. 3) Inference: at maturity, meaning migrates inward as 内教. 4) Inference: ascent to 玄 is loss of coarse grasping including grasping of the path’s shell. 5) Conclusion: salvation logic is pedagogical ascent from outer to inner mystery.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Structure BaZi-guided cultivation in grades: ethics → breath/body → silent mystery. 2) When a client’s chart is ripe (strong resource+output, stable mind markers), shift from ritual quantity to inner quality. 3) Detect ‘stuck on form’ as a new obstacle after early success. 4) Use transitional luck pillars to retire obsolete methods. 5) Keep outer respect for liturgy while not equating it with the summit.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 赤书真文经’s emphasis on cosmic graphs and liturgy, 升玄内教 argues for interiorizing beyond outer codes. It differs from pure neidan manuals by retaining Lingbao graded-church pedagogy. The key thesis is esoteric ascent as curriculum, not denial of the outer.

entries.logic_thesis: The Dingguan Jing proves that liberation follows a law of settled contemplation: first stabilize (定), then observe (观), such that clarity arises from stillness rather than from forced insight. It argues that scattered seeking produces false visions, while correct sequence yields genuine detachment and brightness. Method-order is salvific cause.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the ordinary mind is agitated and mis-sees. 2) Premise: agitation cannot be cured by more conceptual striving. 3) Inference: settle the mind until it holds. 4) Inference: from stability, observation becomes accurate and self-liberating. 5) Conclusion: 定→观 is the necessary logical order of contemplative proof.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For high-fire or kill-heavy BaZi, emphasize 定 first (breath counting, posture) before analysis. 2) For overly sealed/stagnant charts, carefully introduce 观 after minimal stability to avoid dullness. 3) Session design: 2/3 settling, 1/3 observing for beginners. 4) Chart readings only after the reader’s own 定. 5) Track signs: fewer reactive emotions as proof of genuine 定观, not more mystical stories.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 大通经’s brief end-state language, 定观经 specifies the causal sequence of practice. It differs from 明鉴’s mirror imagery by stressing stages of calming before illumined seeing. Its contribution is methodological order as doctrine.

entries.name_han: 太上虚皇天尊四十九章经
entries.logic_thesis: The Forty-nine Chapters prove that the Dao’s teaching can be exhaustively modularized into discrete instructional units, each addressing a facet of mind, world, and liberation under the Xu Huang Heavenly Worthy. It argues that completeness is achieved by traversing a structured curriculum rather than a single slogan. Multiplicity of chapters serves one empty-sovereign source.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: beings’ confusions are many-sided. 2) Premise: a single undifferentiated teaching fails specific diseases of mind. 3) Inference: chaptered instruction covers the field systematically. 4) Inference: practicing chapter by chapter accumulates toward total reorientation. 5) Conclusion: structured plurality is skillful means of the formless 虚皇.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Map 49 thematic modules onto a year-long cultivation calendar. 2) Assign chapters to BaZi weak points (anger chapters for fire excess, etc.). 3) Do not skip to ‘advanced’ chapters without foundation modules. 4) After each chapter-practice, write one behavioral proof. 5) Periodically return to emptiness chapters to prevent modular reification.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike short texts such as 大通经, this work’s logic is encyclopedic pedagogy. It differs from 功过格 by teaching transformative views/practices rather than scoring acts. The distinct claim is curriculum completeness under an empty-imperial deity.

entries.name_han: 太上玄都妙本清净身心经
entries.logic_thesis: This scripture proves that purity of body and mind is recovery of the ‘wondrous root’ (妙本) at the Mysterious Capital—not cosmetic cleanliness. It argues that defilement is adventitious; cleansing reveals the already-pure base. Dual purification (physical and mental) is required because impurity couples across body-mind.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the original root is pure. 2) Premise: postnatal dust settles on body and mind together. 3) Inference: one-sided cleansing (body only or mind only) leaves residual stain. 4) Inference: coordinated purity restores access to 妙本. 5) Conclusion: 清净身心 is ontological recovery, not social hygiene.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Pair hygienic routines with mental confession/release as one protocol. 2) In BaZi toxicity patterns (heavy killing+peer, or wet earth turbidity), design purification seasons. 3) Use simple food, breath, and ethical speech as triple filter. 4) Before major luck-pillar shifts, run a purity retreat to meet new qi cleanly. 5) Evaluate purity by reduced inner noise and fewer self-conflicts, not by performative asceticism.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 除三尸经, the enemy here is defilement-as-dust rather than parasites. It differs from 内观经 by stressing dual body-mind cleansing toward a named 妙本. The logic is root-recovery via purity rather than vision of gods or numeric merit.

entries.logic_thesis: The Nine Cauldron instructions prove that immortality can be engineered through correct external alchemy: materials, fire phases, timing, and vessel order are causal, not mystical wish. It argues that the elixir’s success encodes cosmic process in laboratory operations—failure is procedural error. Transcendence is a technical achievement under Huang-Lao authority.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: minerals and fire can be transmuted under lawlike stages. 2) Premise: the nine-鼎 sequence mirrors perfected cosmic refinement. 3) Inference: precise protocol yields shendan; imprecision yields poison or null. 4) Inference: the perfected elixir transforms the human body-economy. 5) Conclusion: sacred techne is a valid path of transcendence alongside pure meditation.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Read BaZi as ‘furnace conditions’: what fire (motivation/timing), what vessel (constitution), what materials (resources) you have. 2) Apply staged patience—do not jump refining phases in life projects. 3) For modern practitioners, translate external elixir logic into laboratory discipline of sleep, diet, herbs only under safe expertise—or into symbolic neidan firing cycles. 4) Use seasonal nodes as ‘fire times.’ 5) Document each stage; alchemy without records is not alchemy.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 性命圭旨’s internalized dual cultivation, this text centers external laboratory causality. It differs from pure precept or contemplation scriptures by making matter and fire the argument’s heroes. Its logic is operative cosmotechnology rather than moral or purely mental soteriology.

entries.logic_thesis: The Scripture of Inner Contemplation proves that the Dao is found by turning the gaze inward: the body-mind contains the entire field of spirit, and outer seeking multiplies delusion. It argues that correct 内观 reveals emptiness, spirit, and life as already present, converting metaphysics into a perceptual practice. Knowing the Dao is a change of direction of attention.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: the Dao is not a remote object among objects. 2) Premise: outward chase reinforces the split between seeker and sought. 3) Inference: reverse the gaze into the inner domain of spirit and vitality. 4) Inference: sustained inner seeing clarifies original nature and calms destiny-chaos. 5) Conclusion: 内观 is both method and proof of the Dao’s immanence.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Daily reverse-attention drill: from senses → breath → spirit → open awareness. 2) In BaZi counseling, teach clients to observe their chart patterns as inner habits, not only outer events. 3) When 七杀/伤官 agitation is high, use 内观 to metabolize heat before action. 4) Alternate brief outer ritual with longer inner viewing to avoid dependence on spectacle. 5) Criterion of progress: less compulsion to seek signs outside.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 中经’s detailed deity bureaucracy, 内观经 is leaner and more nature-of-mind oriented. It differs from 定观经 by emphasizing the inward turn as such more than the formal 定/观 taxonomy. The core argument is directional: truth is missed by vector, not by lack of information.

entries.logic_thesis: This Zhengyi scripture proves that disruptive agencies (鬼) are real operational factors in illness and chaos, and that correctly authorized spells can command, bind, or expel them. It argues that ritual speech under Zhengyi mandate is not poetry but executive force within a legal-spiritual order. Order is restored when illegitimate spirits are brought under lawful spell-authority.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Premise: many disorders involve intrusive or aggrieved spirit-agencies. 2) Premise: the Zhengyi covenant grants priests command language backed by higher law. 3) Inference: properly formed 咒 apply that law to specific agents. 4) Inference: successful binding/expulsion restores human and communal equilibrium. 5) Conclusion: exorcistic speech is a legitimate causal technology of the Zhengyi path.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi, treat extreme, sudden, anomalous afflictions during void/clash years as candidates for spirit-related differential diagnosis—without neglecting medical care. 2) Only practice spells with lineage authorization; unauthorized imitation breaks the text’s own logic of mandate. 3) Pair expulsions with merit and purification so the vacuum is not refilled. 4) Strengthen the day-master’s ‘right authority’ (healthy officer/seal) as the human side of Zhengyi order. 5) Post-rite, install stable daily regimen; exorcism without re-ordering lifestyle is incomplete.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 内观/定观 contemplative proofs, this text is juridical-exorcistic: power is command under covenant. It differs from 除三尸经 by targeting mostly external/intrusive agencies rather than innate corpses. Its distinctive logic is performative sacred law—speech acts that enforce cosmic police power.
